_meta.name: The Colonel's Take
_meta.note: ORIGINAL lines written in Hannibal Smith's voice. These are NOT quotations from The A-Team and must never be presented as such. Add freely — keys: line, tag.

entries.line: A plan doesn't come together because it's clever. It comes together because somebody kept showing up while it was still ugly.
Everybody wants the part where it works. Nobody signs up for the eleven weeks before that.
You don't need the whole road lit. You need the next hundred feet and a full tank.
Being underestimated is a position, not an insult. Use the cover while you've got it.
If the plan only survives when everything goes right, that's not a plan. That's a wish with a timeline.
Move slow enough that you're deciding, fast enough that you're not negotiating with yourself.
The mission doesn't care how you feel about it at six in the morning.
Improvise the method. Never improvise the objective.
Most operations don't fail at the hard part. They fail because nobody did the boring part first.
You want to know if a plan's any good? Ask what happens when the first piece breaks. Because it will.
Anybody can hold the line on a good day. The whole point is what you do on the bad one.
Quit adding steps. Every step is somewhere it can come apart.
There's a difference between waiting and stalling. One has a trigger. The other has an excuse.
You don't win by being the loudest in the room. You win by being the one who already knows what happens next.
Small team, clear objective, nobody guessing. That beats numbers every time.
If you can't say the objective in one sentence, you haven't got one yet.
Take the shot you've got. The perfect one isn't coming, and the window's closing.
Reputation is built on the jobs nobody watched you finish.
When it goes sideways — and it goes sideways — the only question is how fast you stop arguing with reality.
Rest is part of the operation. A tired man makes expensive decisions.
Don't confuse activity with progress. Plenty of men are busy going nowhere at speed.
You've got one hard thing today. Do it first, while you've still got something to spend.
The other side is counting on you giving up in week three. Be inconvenient.
Contingency isn't pessimism. It's what lets you commit hard to plan A.
Nobody's coming to hand you the assignment. Pick the objective yourself and get moving.
A promise you keep to yourself when nobody's checking — that's the whole thing right there.
Know which fights are worth having. Most of them aren't, and every one costs you the same.
Surprise isn't luck. It's preparation the other side didn't see you doing.
You're not behind. You're partway through something most people never start.
Finish it. An unfinished operation teaches you nothing and costs you everything you already put in.
